said.words: Rootworm and raft traffic, the Panther River fork and pilgrimage to the Root Talk bring it goods.
The Hist, above all.
After the defeat at the Battle of Argonia in 1E 2811 the native armies retreated here.

why: history: nothing built

said.words: Umbriel's path in 4E 48 passed it by.

why: history: nothing built

said.words: Every naheesh in the interior travels to the Root Talk.

why: an occasion of the year, not a standing thing

what: reed huts, mud domes, root-hollow houses; no stone, no wall

said.words: Reed huts, mud domes and root-hollow houses of reed, mud and living wood stand with no new stone and no outward wall, because the marsh is the wall.

what: the old Xanmeer in stone on the north-west edge

said.words: Only the old Xanmeer on the city's north-western edge, left by the ancients, stands in stone.

what: Heart-Mud pools, the landing, plank walks

said.words: Pools of black Heart-Mud lie between the roots, the air is thick and warm, boats tie up at the city landing and plank walks thread the districts.

Overwhelmingly Argonian, drawn from the interior's exclusive breeds: Agaceph on tail-poled rafts, with Paatru and Naga visitors and a very small outsider presence of perhaps a handful, each there on a naheesh's word.
The guard is a tribal levy answerable to the assembly, not to strangers.
Its main source, Helstrom in Black Marsh & Valenwood (Black Marsh.esm), is a town of 308 buildings built in Nordic and Dunmer style with two interiors, one of them an Argonian house.

what: Nordic pieces dropped; houses, landing and ship kept

said.words: Its Nordic and Dunmer pieces are replaced or dropped, and its Argonian houses, landing and moored ship are kept; the ship's hold is the boatmen's lodge.

what: smithy, levy's post, council house, wardens, strongroom

said.words: Lilmoth (King of the Murkmire) supplies the interiors a city needs: its ironworks is set here as the market smithy, its guardhouse as the levy's post, and Dragonthorn Manor as the council house, with its barracks for the wardens and a strongroom behind an added iron door.

what: the city tree, its sap pool and the root landing

said.words: The city tree is King of the Murkmire's Hist in its sap pool, and the root landing is the rootworm's mud mouth among its roots.

The old Xanmeer is Black Marsh & Valenwood's stepped temple on the city's north-western edge; its hall is the throne wing of King of the Murkmire's Teeth of Sithis Halls, copied alone and stripped of its king, guards, traps and treasure; it is lit and has benches for the council's open sittings, while Teku-Sul keeps the whole of that hall, dark, hostile and gated.

what: Lilmoth's healer's hut and apothecary rooms; a hall of living roots

said.words: Still to add: Lilmoth's healer's hut and apothecary as rooms of the tree-minders and the sap-seller, and a tree-minders' hall of living roots in place of the borrowed cave.

why: the tree-minders' hall stands as the source's cave unit with its room (need 9 met); the apothecary sells from the sap stall with the alchemy lab; the healer sells in the hall: the record's later wish, for the owner

Ajum-Teel: maker of fleshfly emollient and scale balm
He boils fleshfly emollient and scale balms for the stall.
He sells most of them to raft crews before the flesh-fly season.
Aleesh-Ta: sap-boiler
Jaxuul-Em's partner, she boils raw sap down in clay pots until it is thick enough to sell, and she watches the fire without ever stepping away.
Aweeta: pitch-boiler
She boils resin into pitch for sealing logs and smells of smoke wherever she goes.
Bakheel-Ne: fruit-picker
Beelum-Sah: feather-trapper
He sets snare lines for fellrunners in the Murkwood and brings their feathers to the household's stall before the market opens.
Bexeeh-Tul: apprentice smith
He works the bellows and the grindstone at the smithy and is learning the forge from his father.
Chaleeka: nest-finder
She wades the reed beds ahead of her father looking for new nests, and she can read a bird's movements from a bent stalk.
Cheeval-Xu: rootworm handler at the root landing
He keeps the root landing, where travellers climb down to board the rootworms.
Chuxee: market stall-hand
She minds the household's stall at the market, weighs out the cakes and remembers who owes what.
Dasheel-Ko: reed-mat weaver
He cuts and weaves river reeds into the sleeping mats that half the stilt houses of the district lie on.
Deetsa-Hul: porter at the landing
She hauls cargo from the rafts to the market stalls.
In the pilgrim season she works from first light until after dark.
Dru-Kaleel: feather-sorter
Beelum-Sah's father, he sorts the trapped feathers by length and sheen, light work he took up when his knees would no longer carry him into the wood.
Ekaneesh: grave-singer
She is a grave-singer.
She stakes the city's dead and sings the final song over them.
Eleexa-Bur: Heart-Mud digger
She digs black Heart-Mud from the pools between the roots and packs it into the walls of the city's houses.
Epeela: basket-weaver
Dasheel-Ko's mother, she weaves the small baskets from the leavings of his mats, as she has always done.
Fuleeka: bone-needle carver
Xaleet-Ur's mother, she carves needles and awls from bone, light work she is proud of and sells by the handful.
Gahzeel: the city levy, night watch
He guards the streets by night for the levy and sleeps at its camp.
Gathe-Ru: cook to the council house
Born in Pusbottom, she cooks for the council house and sleeps in a room of the council house.
She owes a Lilmoth moneylender more than a cook can pay.
Gaxeel-Oru: river fisher
He casts his nets from the same stilt landing his father did and sells the catch to the market's stalls each dawn.
Gojeel-Mur: leather-lacer
He laces the tanned strips into sheaths and satchels, and a market stall sells his work at twice what he is paid.
Haj-Teesh: the city levy, warden of the council house by night
He keeps the night's watch on the council house and the key to nothing but his own sword; the strongroom's key stays with the treasurer.
Hameel-Jo: raft-builder
He lashes raft logs together on the river bank, and rafts of his go as far as the delta with other men's goods.
Hazeeka: trodh fisher
She fishes the slow backwaters for trodh with her father and keeps the best of each catch for her mother's table.
Heeshu: sap-gatherer
She collects the sap that the tree-minders release for sale and carries it home in sealed gourds.
Heetaxi: resin-caulker
He seals roofs and raft seams with Hist-sap resin.
He works in the dry spells and sits idle through the monsoon.
Hixee-Ra: naheesh of the assembly
She is a naheesh and sits with the city's assembly of elders and tree-minders.
She knows the sacred croaks of the Root Talk by heart.
Hulun-Kesh: the city levy, night watch
He guards the streets by night in his turn with the city levy.
He lodges with the boatwoman's household.
Hurixa-Pen: dyer of reed mats
Dasheel-Ko's partner, she dyes his mats with swamp roots and bark so that no two houses end up with the same pattern.
Huzeel-Tan: grave-stake carver
He carves the grave-stakes that the city's grave-singers set over the dead.
Imeel-Vah: stall-runner
The youngest, she runs between the house and the stall with fresh cakes and learns every customer's face.
Ishaxa: arrow-fletcher
Jaxuul-Em: sap-gatherer
He taps the sap-trees of the Murkwood at dawn and has done so since he was a boy, and the sap-seller buys the best of his jars.
Jeelixus: trodh fisher
He nets trodh in the shallows of the river fork and sells them live at the market.
Jeenaxi: egg-tender
She tends the eggs in the city's nest-pools and records every clutch with its parents and its hatch date.
Juxee-Meen: pickler of frog's eyes
Kassa-Weel: porter, working off an Owing
She owes a season of labour to a household that she wronged, by the ruling of the assembly's naheesh.
She carries loads at the landing and keeps nothing of her pay until the season ends.
Kehluk-Aa: egg-gatherer
He poles into the reed beds at first light to gather eggs from the nests and knows every colony within a morning's reach.
Ketsu-Lan: feather carrier
She carries bundled feathers to the market and to the dyers by plank walk, and she knows which stalls pay late.
Kuxeesh: pilgrim host and river fisher
He takes in pilgrims for the Root Talk through the month of Hist-Tsoko.
The rest of the year he fishes the river.
Kuzuul-Se: reed-cutter
She wades into the reed beds at low water and cuts the long stalks for her father's mats, and has never once been bitten.
Lassi-Oom: thatch-layer
She lays reed thatch on the stilt houses of the district and is on a roof most days before the sun is.
Leeshaa: stew-pot keeper
Zhasa-Lok's mother, she keeps the household's stew pot simmering at the hearth and adds to it until it is a week old.
Lieshu: herb-gatherer
She gathers herbs and roots in the swamp around the city for the household's stall.
Lumeexa: lumberry gatherer and cook
She gathers lumberries in Last Seed and cooks for the pilgrims who lodge with her household.
Meeja-Tsoi: pilgrim guide
She meets the pilgrims who come for the Root Talk in Hist-Tsoko and finds them floor space in the city.
Meesha-Rul: egg-carrier at the market
Kehluk-Aa's partner, she carries the eggs to the market and lays them in reed baskets so none break, and she never haggles twice over the same dozen.
Meshu-Ka: Root-Folk smith at the market smithy
He works the forge at the market smithy with iron bought from the raft crews.
The levy and the raft crews buy his blades and fittings and pay him well in goods.

Meshu-Ka trades: the Root-Folk smith at the market smithy, who works iron bought from the raft crews: iron, steel, hide and leather made here and in number, the city's own pattern at T3, one far-carried piece at T4; vanilla's blacksmith gold 1000 times P4's 1.25; within P4's list value 3000
Mulaxi-Re: fish-smoker
She smokes the catch over a root-wood fire so it keeps for the river traders, and she knows every fisher's boat by the smell of its fish.
Naseeta-Bo: tanner
Xaleet-Ur's partner, she tans the hides he cures and sells the leather in strips to those who make straps and sheaths.
Neeshal: tanner
He tans hides at the smithy's rack and cuts leather straps for his partner's fittings.
Neeta-Pho: snare-minder's helper
The youngest, she runs the short snare lines near the city's edge and brings back what the trapper cannot carry.
Neeza-Kai: the city levy, warden of the council house by night
She came to the wardens from the city levy and still drills with them on her days off.
Nesh-Deeka: handler of the Toh-Reel-Ka, known in the city as a tally-keeper of goods landed at the river fork
She writes down every cargo landed at the river fork and who carried it, and keeps her tallies at the table of a quiet house by the city landing.
Visitors come to her by word of mouth, and few in the city could say whose house it is.
Never-Writes-Twice: officer of the Toh-Reel-Ka over Nesh-Deeka, known in the city as a raft-pilot
She lodges in Nesh-Deeka's house and stands at the back of its room whenever the order has work there; in the city she passes for a raft-pilot from the northern rivers.
Nine-Teeth: the city levy, night watch
She lost nine teeth in a fight on the plank walks and has been called Nine-Teeth since.
She guards the streets by night for the levy.
Nobu-Seeth: pole-whittler
Pessa-Kur's father, he whittles the long poles raft-hands push with; the work is light and he does it sitting by the water.
Nolu-Jeel: builder of plank walks
He builds the plank walks and stilt footings between the districts of the city.
He also trains living wood into walkway posts, which takes years.
Nuexa-Lei: feather-dresser
She cleans, sorts and bundles the fellrunner feathers that the hunters of Murkwood bring to the household's stall.
Nuxeeka: feather-trapper
She traps fellrunners in Murkwood for their feathers and sells them to the stalls at the market.
Ohanga-Tsei: net-mender
She poled rafts on the Panther River for most of her life.
Now she mends nets on the household's landing.
Okaw-Neesa: net-maker
She is the mother of Poles-Upriver and knots fishing nets for the city's river fishers.
She poled rafts herself until her grip failed.
Okeem-Zuul: the city levy, warden of the council house by night
He was a raft-guard on the southern rivers before the council took him on to walk the council house's stilts by night.
Oleeka-Tsun: depth-stick carver
She carves depth sticks and sells them to visitors who do not know the city's pools.
Ooleesha: net-mender
Gaxeel-Oru's mother, she sits at the door with a bone needle and mends what the river tears; her fingers are slow now but never wrong.
Oomee-Tal: cook of lumberry cakes
Zhasa-Lok's partner, she bakes lumberries into dense cakes that keep for the rafts, and she sells out before noon.
Ooxa-Leet: naheesh of the assembly
Opaxi: reed-basket weaver
He weaves the baskets his father and mother carry the eggs in, and no basket of his has ever leaked a yolk.
Paxu-Lei: scale-groomer
She works from a mat beside the market.
Pessa-Kur: rope-twister
Hameel-Jo's partner, she twists the bark rope that holds each of his rafts together and sells the spare coils to the landing.
Poles-Upriver: raft-master at the city landing
She poles a cargo raft from Helstrom to the river villages of Truowa, Korydon, Marzai and Julo.
Raxeela-Hut: the city levy, day watch
She serves the day watch of the levy and lodges with Kuxeesh's household.
At the landing she searches every outsider's pack.
Rilsa-Wen: raft-hand
She poles the finished rafts to the landing for the boatmen and is saving for a raft of her own.
Ruusa-Wan: lets a room behind the market's stalls
She keeps a quiet room behind the market's stalls and lets it only to those who give the right word; two lanterns on her sill mean the room is free.
Ruweel-Ta: the city levy, day watch
He walks the day watch of the city levy and lodges with the trader's household.
He stops outsiders at the landing and does not explain why.
Ruxa-Neel: water-carrier
She carries river water to the houses near the market in the weeks when the city spring is left untouched.
Ruzeel-Ai: hide-scraper
She scrapes the hides clean before her mother tans them and has hands the colour of old bark from it.
Sakka-Zuul: the city levy, day watch
He serves the day watch of the levy and lodges with the sap-seller.
He was a raftsman before his tribe sent him to serve his turn.
Saxeena: plank-walk mender
She mends the plank walks between the districts and replaces the boards that have rotted in the wet.
Seesa-Lur: the city levy, warden of the council house by night
She watches the back door to the river landing and counts the rafts that tie up below it after dark.
Shuxeeta: porter at the landing
She unloads rafts at the landing and carries the goods to the households.
The naheesh of the assembly set the share that each household receives.
Sleeps-Last: keeper of the boatmen's lodge
He keeps the boatmen's lodge, where raft crews and the few outsiders eat and sleep.
The crews named him for being the last awake in the lodge each night.
Sleeps-Last trades: the boatmen's lodge, where raft crews and the few outsiders eat: food of the city's own goods, nothing significant; vanilla's inn gold 100 times P4's 1.25
Soorka: jar-sealer
Jaxuul-Em's mother, she seals each finished jar with wax and reed, a light task she keeps because she will not stop working.
Taleeka-Ma: tree-minder and healer; sells Restoration and Alteration tomes
She is a tree-minder of the city grove and heals the sick at the tree-minders' hall.
She sells tomes of Restoration and Alteration and teaches healing to those who ask.

Taleeka-Ma trades: the tree-minder and healer: tomes of Restoration and Alteration to Adept, as the place record lists them, a few magicka draughts; vanilla's spell vendor gold 500 times P4's 1.25; within P4's list value 3000
Taxeel-Wan: fisher; serves turns in the levy
He fishes with his mother between his turns in the levy.
He serves his next turn in Hist-Tsoko, when pilgrims crowd the city.
Teexu-Ri: raft-builder's apprentice
The youngest, she carries tools and lashes knots badly but quickly, and the builder lets him try again.
Tsaxi-Rei: rootworm courier
He rides the rootworms through the tunnels of the Hist roots to the villages of the basin.
He brings back orders for the stall.
Tseeja-Num: sinker-stone shaper
Gaxeel-Oru's partner, he chips river stones into the weights that hold the household's nets down, and he sells the spares to other fishers.
Tsiraxi: river fisher
She fishes the river fork from a one-person raft and sells her catch at the market.
Tsoonu-Ba: jar carrier
The youngest, he carries jars to the market and brings back the coin in a knotted cord he is proud to be trusted with.
Tuxeel-Ra: the city levy, warden of the council house by night
He keeps the gallery side of the house and sleeps through the day's noise of the hall below.
Tzalun: the city levy, leads the day watch
He is the oldest of the levy at the camp and leads the day watch.
He settles quarrels among the guards before the naheesh hear of them.
Ulxaa-Tem: nest-basket minder
The youngest, she minds the nest baskets by the door and counts them morning and night.
Uxal-Dee: the city levy, night watch
He guards the streets by night for the city levy and lodges at the smith's house.
Veexa-Oon: sap-gatherer's apprentice
She climbs after her father to the high taps and is learning which trees are rested and which are tired.
Vexaa: curing-frame minder
The youngest, she tends the curing frames and shoos the flies off with a palm frond.
Vuh-Jeedus: the city levy, warden of the council house by night
The youngest warden, set to stand before the strongroom's iron door until dawn.
Wahzeel: snare-maker
She twists the snare cords that her father's lines depend on, and she can tell a fraying cord by sound alone.
Weeruk-Ta: bark-shingle cutter
He learned the trade on his father's crew.
Weetsa: egg-gatherer
She gathers marsh-bird eggs in the forest around the city for the household's stall.
She goes out at first light and is back before the market opens.
Weighs-Every-Coin: market trader in Murkwood feathers, sap, eggs and river fish
She buys from the raft crews and the rootworm riders and sells Murkwood feathers, sap, eggs and river fish from her market stall.

Weighs-Every-Coin trades: the market trader in Murkwood feathers, sap, eggs and river fish (the economy note): the city's own goods first and in number, a few carried-in things; vanilla's general gold 750 times P4's 1.25;
T1 to T3, within P4's list value 3000
Wethu-Zan: reed-sorter
The youngest, he sorts the cut reeds by length and thickness, and is quicker at it than he lets on.
Wujeel: sap and herb seller; teaches alchemy
He sells Hist-sap and swamp herbs from a stall with an alchemy bench and teaches the craft to apprentices who can pay.
Sap is dear in Helstrom, because the tree-minders allow little to be taken.

Wujeel trades: the sap and herb seller: sap and swamp herbs made here first and in number, then the draughts he brews from them, fewer of each tier upward; vanilla's apothecary gold 500 times P4's 1.25; within P4's list value 3000
Xaleet-Ur: hide-curer
He cures river-beast hides on racks above the water and sells them to the city's tanner and cobbler.
Xeeko-Dul: fish-gutter, learning the nets
The youngest of the house, he guts the day's catch at the landing and is learning to throw a net as straight as his father.
Xilsa-Jee: root-tender, learning the tree-minder's work
She is learning the tree-minder's work from her mother.
She clears rot and creepers from the roots of the grove.
Xuhal-Teeus: raft-builder
He builds the rafts for his partner's trade, lashing cane and sealing the joints with Hist-sap resin.
Yeelu: potter of sap jars
She shapes and fires the household's clay jars, and every jar of hers carries a thumbprint at the base.
Zeexa-Num: frog-catcher
She catches chirping frogs on the Panther River fork and sells them by their tone to the makers of frog pipes.
Zhasa-Lok: lumberry gatherer
He picks lumberries from the root-hollows that other gatherers pass by, and he sells them fresh at the market each morning.
Ziru-Neem: egg-tender
Kehluk-Aa's mother, she minds the eggs the household sets aside to hatch, and she hums to them when the house is quiet.

said.words: The city's alleys are as dangerous as they are fine, and its guard has a bad name.
Helstrom does not trade outward; it receives and redistributes, because the rivers all drain to it.
Its market traders sell Murkwood feathers, sap, eggs and river fish.

Helstrom's city tree and its tree-minders matter more than any office, and the Root Talk, the occasion at which the Hist's alignment becomes audible to all the tribes, is held here in the holy month Hist-Tsoko.
A stranger stranded on the approaches is pulled out by an Agaceph raftsman.
A quiet house by the city landing takes visitors only by word of mouth, and nobody will say whose it is.
It meets the Root Talk and is run by its own people, not by any distant government.
The assembly of naheesh and tree-minders decides by consensus.
